summary: Two-project integration brief: Tool Gate is a Rust library/CLI that evaluates caller-supplied tool metadata and invocation envelopes and emits allow, deny, or review-required receipts without executing tools (README.md:5-13). Agent Loop proposes autonomous work, while Tool Gate provides the deterministic pre-execution decision layer (README.md:51-56). Their shared safety boundary is the transition from an agent-proposed action to runtime permission and side effects (README.md:17-20). Recommendation: require every Agent Loop tool proposal to pass through Tool Gate and permit runtime execution only for a validated allow receipt; route review_required receipts to an operator. Tool Gate risk: it trusts caller-supplied metadata and is not a sandbox, authentication system, or execution runtime, so dishonest metadata or bypassing callers can undermine policy (README.md:10-13,156-158). Agent Loop risk: proposed work could reach execution without deterministic policy enforcement if the runtime allows agents to bypass the gate (README.md:31-33). The declared clean-tree check succeeded, and no files were modified.
